_note: supcon_ce_convnext_base (Run 1: SupCon model): SupCon (crop + disease) plus cross-entropy heads, the same recipe as the previous model's best run, on the same backbone as the independent CNN baseline (the model itself is the SupCon model, not that baseline): ConvNeXt-Base (timm convnext_base.fb_in22k_ft_in1k, ImageNet-22k pretraining). Settings follow config/baseline/aniq_baseline_independent_convnext_base.json where this trainer supports them: bicubic resizing, crop scale 0.5-1.0, lr 5e-5 backbone / 5e-4 heads, weight decay 0.05, drop path 0.1, head dropout 0.2. Differences: no warmup or gradient clipping, SupCon batch of 64 images (128 views) instead of an effective batch of 32, and the SupCon loss itself. Epoch and gamma are chosen on 3 validation splits built from train only. Compare against the independent ConvNeXt-Base baseline (same backbone), Hein's package result (HM 71.44%) and the multi-task ConvNeXt baseline.
_result: Run 1: SupCon model. Test HM Top-1 66.0 / Top-5 92.9; seen 54.5, unseen 83.6 (calibrated); raw seen 71.3, raw unseen 7.2; 32.9% of seen images sent to unseen pairs. Epoch 6, gamma 6.75, validation HM 59.2 (per split 53.6 / 59.4 / 64.5). Below the independent ConvNeXt-Base baseline from independent_cnn_baseline (HM 71.44, seen 67.0, unseen 76.5): the gap is on seen accuracy; unseen is higher. Diagnostic only (test-set sweep, not used for selection): best gamma 6.0 would give HM 68.4, and the HM curve is steep around the optimum.

model._note: ConvNeXt-Base from timm, ImageNet-22k pretraining then 1k fine-tuning; drop_path_rate is stochastic depth. ce_dropout matches the baseline's head dropout.

input._note: Bicubic resizing, as ConvNeXt was pretrained.

augmentation._note: Same as the independent ConvNeXt-Base baseline.

loss._note: CHANGED: total = SupCon(crop) + SupCon(disease) + ce_weight * (CE(crop) + CE(disease)). Label smoothing as in the baselines.

scoring._note: CHANGED: mode heads, the cross-entropy heads' log-probabilities. temperature is only used for the prototypes saved alongside.

optimizer._note: As the independent ConvNeXt-Base baseline (lr_head also covers the projection and cross-entropy heads).

runtime._note: grad_checkpointing: recompute backbone activations in the backward pass; identical gradients, less GPU memory, somewhat slower. Needed because ConvNeXt-Base with 128 views per step did not fit in 16 GB.
